When you read the full statement in the English translation what it says is, as Defence Counsel correctly quoted: "Mr. Delalic did not introduce himself to me but I knew from many other people his position was". I think your Honours would certainly be able to infer -- what the Prosecution would believe is probably the witness said was something like: "He did not introduce his position to me", and it is just an interpretation issue. It is not necessarily that one is right and one is wrong. That's one of the reasons why the Prosecution wishes the statements to be introduced, so your Honours can look at them and determine whether or not you believe it's likely that there may have been an interpretation issue or whether or not, in fact, the witness said this, or something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But when the members from the OTP examined these persons -- when the members from the OTP examine these witnesses, don't they keep the record of the statement in their own language?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: No, your Honour. At least up until any investigation that I have worked on, which has been several, not just Celebici, but for a while I haven't been working on any new investigations, so unless something has changed, which I know at various times there are talk about how best to handle this issue, it is the case that the statement is taken in English, because the person taking the statement, the investigator, does not speak Serbo-Croatian. So the statement is taken in English and there is no original Serbo-Croatian to maintain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But don't you audio record his statement which he is making to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Video or cassette, do you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just cassette.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: In the past that has not been the case. I don't know if that is the case with investigations that are on-going. I can certainly say with respect to this case none of the -- unless someone was interviewed and advised of their rights, which is the case with some people, in which case those interviews are audio recorded, there are no recordings made. It is just the written statement in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But this is very interesting. The witness is asked to certify that this is a correct statement but in a language which he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How can he read it?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: What the witness attests to is -- JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: A translated version of what he said.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Exactly. Let me find it for your Honours. What the witness attests to is the statement that has been read to him in whatever language is true, and then the interpreter then certifies that: "I am a qualified translator and I have translated this", but it certainly is an issue. What we have here is -- then when it is translated back into Serbo-Croatian what you have is a translation of a translation, which causes additional problems. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Actually this matter has been discussed for quite a while. It was impossible in the field to do otherwise except you have somebody who can take it down in that language and keep it in that language for the purposes of the trial, but I don't know how to. This still creates problems. All it might do at this stage, it might create doubts in the mind of whoever is considering his statement as to how much he can rely on those statements. This is perhaps what it might do. Well, I know those are some of the hazards of a trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, can't you take advantage of the certificate which the translator gives on the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Instead of calling the translator, the certificate is there and the Prosecution does not dispute that the certificate is that of the translator.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: We of course do that, as Mr. Greaves did today. I don't know. My guess is there is a whole bunch of translators sitting around this building saying: "I wish they'd stop doing this to us. We would love to get in there and tell the judges we do this right and we are good at what we do" but I understand they are not permitted to testify under the rules that exist here at the present time. I am just raising what I think is a problem and I'm hoping that some thought can be given to it beyond: "There's nothing we can do about it". I think maybe there is something we can do about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I would suggest because all of these translators are certified by the Registry of the Tribunal that that is at least conclusive evidence -- it may be rebuttal, but at least a rebuttal presumption that, in fact, they did their job, they did their job like they were supposed to and they did it competently. If someone says it is a bad translation, it would be the burden of the person to prove it, not just to claim it, but to bring forward proof that the translation isn't accurate. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Thank you very much. Actually in all literary things the problem of translation has been very well understood and known. When you translate from one translation to the other, and it depends on who translates, and as many people have translated particular subject matter have what they call their own influence on it. Even if you call someone else to translate the same thing, they might not use the same words. So it is not that one can categorically say you can do, but an effort will be made to make sure there is a minimum of acceptance which one can get to translations, because it is not the words of the person who has spoken the original thing and he might not use the words that the translator has used, and another translator might not even use the same words. So we are still going from one to the other. It's a pity but we will try. It is a process of learning. At some stage we will find a solution. Now I think we will now adjourn until 4th August and for that week we will sit only until 7th August and resume again on 11th-15th. I think that's the next schedule when we resume. So I wish everyone a good holiday. (3.30 pm)
